item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching The Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 8
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 8 twice.

Well, this episode was probably just a side story in the Verdigris House. Maomao's dad was really good, but it was hard to confirm he was right. She might have imagined he was that good and that he was able to guess it from only a small amount of evidence, though he didn't say a word. And also, why didn't he say anything other than asking her a couple of questions? So, I couldn't figure out whether he was really that talented or not. Also, from the result of Maomao's conjecture, it would have been almost magic if he had deduced it. There were 2 drinks and I couldn't figure it out until she worked it through. That said, he didn't receive the money, which included a hush-money fee. So he might have known that at least that person was suspicious. So, they all planned to poison him.

In terms of Jinshi, he got so upset that it was great to watch, and he showed some emotions he had never shown on his face. So, by episode 8, he had already fallen in love with Maomao, obviously, not just interested in her. And obviously, she was probably the only one he couldn't charm at all, because everyone else was attracted to Jinshi for his high rank and how cool he was. Maomao was so dense, or just avoided thinking about it unconsciously, so it would take more time for him to date her. Gyokuyou found it so funny and laughed a lot when she overheard the exchange between him and Maomao. Assuming he was the Emperor's brother, for Gyokuyou, he was like a brother-in-law, though she wasn't the Empress. So, she might have felt he was like a child, and she was happy to see Jinshi act his age.

Scores

  • Episode: 7/10
  • Maomao: 7/10
    • She respected and tried to learn things from her dad, and was honest with him
    • She didn't give a hoot about Jinshi at all
    • I was impressed with Aoi Yuki's voice actingg to talk in a low pitch when she treated the two people
  • Maomao's Dad: 5/10
    • He was so quiet and didn't put much into words for Maomao
  • Jinshi: 8/10
    • His shock at what Maomao said was a good one
  • Lady Gyokuyou: 8/10
    • She enjoyed the funny exchange between Jinshi and Maomao like a friend hearing a funny story
  • Lihaku: 5/10
    • A normal person who was attracted to a courtesan

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching The Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 7
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 7 twice.

The episode started the day after the garden party in the previous episode. I wondered where Maomao was sleeping in such a good bed, but it was one of the rooms in the Jade Pavilion.

It was rare that Maomao and Gaoshun talked about issues without Jinshi, so it felt odd to me. But Jinshi seemed to be wiped out, so Gaoshun needed to do it by himself. Also, it was originally her own request, so it made sense. Maomao thought Lady Lishu couldn't read the room at first, but she figured out it was because she was bullied. So, it was great that that first impression actually had a reason behind it. Jinshi also showed his lazy, easygoing side to Gaoshun. Yeah, that was a young man who acts sociable for other people. When Gyokuyou teased him, he was so upset and she found it so funny. It was nice to see her like that.

Lihaku was also a character who gave a hairpin to every girl but didn't take it seriously. Well, but he wasn't really a kind guy and he did that for... why? I don't know. Anyhow, that was good for Maomao, because she didn't care about him at all. She also negotiated well because she showed the hairpins she had received from other people, as if she had more options. In fact, the other two wouldn't have been interested in the same invitation. But he was a man, so he couldn't turn down an invitation to the Verdigris House. I also wondered whether her gift was too generous just to get herself home, but it turned out the madam had thought it through and wanted to attract more loyal customers.

Maomao's adoptive father wasn't surprised at all when he saw her. I guess the madam of the Verdigris House let him know what had happened to Maomao, because Maomao had been sending letters to her, not to him. So, he didn't look all that pleased, but he was quietly happy and listened to her.

I wonder how much of Maomao's conjecture is actually true. I don't remember what actually happened, so it's going to be fun to watch it.

Scores

  • Episode: 7/10
  • Maomao: 7/10
    • She took care of Lady Lishu's food taster regardless of what she did, because their lives were "expendable". She was kind and forgiving to many people
    • She can lift fingerprints like a detective, and she can negotiate like a sales representative.
  • Jinshi: 8/10
    • Showed a different side of him — lazy and easygoing
  • Gaoshun: 7/10
    • How old was he? He knew Jinshi from the start, so he must be old.
    • He was so mature and got along with Jinshi and Maomao well
  • Lady Gyokuyou: 8/10
    • She had a playful side, so she teased Jinshi and enjoyed it
  • Lihaku: 6/10
    • He gave out hairpins for some reason, but it was only superficial
    • He also didn't want to give Maomao the time of day, so he wasn't kind or nice

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching The Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 6
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 6 twice. From this episode, things got complicated and interesting.

I wondered in the previous episode why Lady Lishu wore a different color from her ladies-in-waiting — dark pink, while they wore white. But Maomao mentioned it, though there was no answer for that, so we may be able to figure it out later.

I wonder how many hairpins each person has. Lihaku had many of them, so there was no limit, but I don't think someone like Lihua gave them to many random people. And also, why did Lihaku want to give them to that many people? I forgot.

It was odd that Consort Lishu had been a consort of the previous Emperor — the current Emperor's stepmother, in effect — when she was younger. I mean, why did the previous Emperor marry a nine-year-old girl? It sounded like there was a war between Lishu's original country and that country, and she was married to the previous Emperor to make peace between those countries. Will we know the details later?

In terms of food tasting, this episode really showed how Maomao was off her rocker when it came to poisons. She knew she needed to lie down and felt like a dog after taking poison, but she still loved it and wanted to swallow it. I guess it was like alcohol for her. The other food taster was really scared of eating the food, and it made sense as it's hard to tell whether a dish contains poison. And if they eat a lot, they may kick the bucket. Maomao also thought a food taster was expendable. This scene was great as many series do not care how these high-ranking people avoided poisons, and in this series, we can feel it.

Well, in terms of Lady Lishu and her ladies-in-waiting, was it intentional, and did Lady Lishu have to eat the mackerel? The lady-in-waiting's face obviously showed she knew it, so she was scared when Maomao intimidated her. If your food taster doesn't stop you from eating the poison, and you're in a situation where you're forced to eat, that's a terrible situation. Why didn't people stop this custom, honestly? I guess a few of them died at these garden parties in the past.

There was no brother of the Emperor at the party, but considering Gaoshun was high-ranking and he followed Jinshi, it was obvious that Jinshi was the Emperor's brother. I didn't remember exactly, but I thought he was the son of the Emperor, the next Emperor. Maomao somehow didn't think deeply when it came to him. Maybe she didn't care about him at all.

Scores

  • Score: 8/10
  • Maomao: 9/10
    • Aoi Yuki's voice acting was so good in the details. I was able to feel different small emotions from different behaviors.
    • This was mainly an episode about her as a food taster, and it showed how talented and crazy she was
    • Also she helped Lady Lishu, and she was nice to the ladies-in-waiting from the Crystal Pavilion by giving them warm stones so they didn't get cold
  • Jinshi: 8/10
    • He showed his anxiety about Maomao and took the lead not to let her take any dangerous action
  • Lady Lishu: N/A
    • She had an allergy to mackerel
    • She was in a very tough position with the Emperor
  • Lihaku: N/A
  • Ladies-in-waiting of Gyokuyou:
    • Yinghua: 6/10
      • She was passionate and loved her fellow ladies-in-waiting, like Maomao

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching The Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 5
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 5 twice. When I first watched it, I didn't fully understand what was happening.

I don't understand but somehow matsutake mushrooms were rare and hard to eat. And they ate them just grilled with some salt, and they were so satisfied with them. Are they really that tasty?

Also, for people who lacked knowledge of chemistry or any education, it might've been natural that a fire changing color was a scary thing. That said, I didn't get how they sent secret messages with them. Anyhow, that will be figured out somehow in a future episode, and I don't remember this wooden tablet stuff.

The quack doctor seemed to help Jinshi happily, but he couldn't. This already indicated how high his rank was, and people wanted to get brownie points from him.

The second half was about preparing for a garden party held before the Emperor and getting everyone made up. When Jinshi heard from Maomao that she had been putting on makeup to add freckles because she wanted to avoid danger, he was shocked. He hadn't imagined how poor or ordinary people lived. That meant he had been entirely protected by others, living in a cage of his own — just like the rear palace. He clearly showed his frustration. And I forgot what the hairpin from him meant at the garden party.

When I first watched it, I didn't notice that Maomao mentioned it was going to be a windy day, and she prepared for the cold. So, even though it looked beautiful, I'd wondered why there were so many leaves blowing through the air during the garden party and nobody cared. I was glad the story had already explained it.

Scores

  • Score: 5/10
  • Maomao: 7/10
    • Many people tried to make her eat a lot to get fat healthy
    • As usual. Everyone asked her for a lot of things, and she worked hard.
    • Smart. Figuring out some weird thing from a couple of pieces of information. Doing her usual Maomao thing
  • Jinshi: 7/10
    • Training with a man who was powerful, and showing off his own skill
    • Frustrated by the fact that Maomao had been kidnapped
  • Gyokuyou: 8/10
    • Gorgeous, mysterious robes.
    • She also cared about her ladies-in-waiting and didn't want others to take them away
  • Gaoshun: N/A
  • Quack doctor: 5/10
    • Wanted to get brownie points from Jinshi. Grilled matsutake mushrooms with Maomao, without knowing they hadn't been obtained properly
  • Ladies-in-waiting of Gyokuyou:
    • The passionate lady-in-waiting was good. She had real passion

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 5
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 5 twice. 8/10. It seemed like this episode was meant to wrap up what happened after Rudeus came back to his mansion from the labyrinth.

Elinalise settled down with Cliff, instead of staying an adventurer. Cliff is a member of the Milis Church, but I don't think she is. I forgot about it, but she has a curse. How can she deal with it?

Also, the episode explained that there was no wedding of Rudeus and Roxy because the Migurd don't have that custom. So, this was the first episode that Roxy dressed up in something special at the wedding of Cliff and Elinalise, and it was so cute. She looked like a very cute kid.

Then what Rudy didn't do was throw Norn and Aisha their birthday celebrations. And he had a good memory and remembered the promise he had made with Paul about throwing a big party. And now he was responsible as the head of the Greyrats, so he planned and prepared it. When he was fishing with Norn, Aisha, and Roxy, he couldn't catch any fish, just a boot, so he cast a spell to catch fish. Even Roxy was a little disgusted with him. So, he had grown up a lot as the head of the Greyrats, but he still showed his childish side.

Roxy, on the other hand, still had a couple of challenges. Well, she was more like an introvert. Norn had a problem with her being Rudy's second wife, so Roxy wanted to get along with her, and fishing was her chance. I think she liked helping others, so it worked well and she taught Norn a few techniques. Also, she couldn't buy a hat when she found a good one. It was because the hat was too expensive. And Rudy and Sylphie bought and gave it to her as a wedding gift. That conversation between Sylphie and Roxy was, well, the polygamy point of view, so it was still kinda off to a monogamous person. But Sylphie really loved Rudy, and she was thankful to Roxy too. Roxy may still have felt awkward around her as the second wife, so I guess that was another thing she solved in the scene. Roxy's animation when she got the new hat from Sylphie was very detailed and well framed, so some of the animators must have liked this scene.

Zenith's behavior also improved a little, and she patted Norn's head and held Lilia's hand. Though, I don't know whether she'll ever fully recover, or when. Was her condition caused by magic, or by some other power? No idea how she'll turn out later.

I don't know what'll happen in the next episode. Apparently, Sara will show up again, so Rudy will probably get a job, maybe taking one from a guild. More than that, no idea. And I also have no idea when Rudy'll meet Eris next.

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching The Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 4
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 4 twice. 8/10. This story was about curing Lady Lihua.

The Emperor asked Maomao to cure Lady Lihua, and he said she was a famous apothecary. But until episode 3, Maomao mostly communicated with only a few people: Lady Gyokuyou, Jinshi, Gaoshun, and the quack doctor. So, he had likely heard about Maomao from both Gyokuyou and Jinshi? That means Jinshi was definitely close to him. When Maomao talked to the Emperor, she was trying not to look at him. When she tested food for poison, she always looked down, or looked to the side instead of looking straight ahead, and she even closed her eyes. So, it's obvious that, culturally, most people weren't allowed to look at the Emperor's face directly.

When I first watched this episode, I thought Lady Lihua's ladies-in-waiting were so ignorant and kept using the poisonous powder on Lihua. It was obvious that they didn't believe that the powder was poisonous and kept using it even though it was illegal. When Jinshi talked about the number of Gyokuyou's ladies-in-waiting and said they were wise, it meant that those in the Crystal Pavilion weren't wise. Apparently, that was true. They didn't treat Maomao well either, even though she had come to the Pavilion on the Emperor's orders. So, they were naturally closed off to outsiders and arrogant.

In this episode, Jinshi helped Maomao in two ways instead of doing nothing. First, he helped Maomao get closer to Lihua. Second, he arranged a steam bath. So even though he said Maomao completed the Emperor's mission on her own, that wasn't quite true. And I found it a little strange that he thought so.

Maomao also took care of Lady Lihua for a few months, and she did many things by herself. She proved again that she was talented and a hard worker.

    • Got seriously angry at someone who was doing something wrong

    • Moved other people the way she wanted
  • Jinshi: 7/10
    • Helped Maomao from behind the scenes, or helped a little, when she had trouble

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 3
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 3 twice. 7/10.

This was a sleepwalking lady's story. OK, I didn't notice at first, but Jinshi got a letter from the military officer, so he suspected Concubine Fuyou had lied. And that was the reason he wasn't convinced by Maomao's suggestion. So, he wanted to make sure and tried to work out what kind of person Maomao was.

Also, Maomao started wondering who the hell he was. Of course, she was smart, and he freely walked around the rear palace, so that was very natural. Her conjecture was also somewhat true. He was definitely the Emperor's favorite. She also knew a lot of people and cases in the Verdigris House and remembered them. She was curious about everything but gossip.

But why was Lady Gyokuyou envious of Concubine Fuyou? Didn't she have someone she wanted to be with, even though she was with the Emperor? Maybe it was a lot of pressure to be one of the Emperor's concubines.

It was good that the quack doctor had already forgiven Maomao as well. He might've been afraid of someone who didn't know medicines touching anything in his storeroom.

And then, why was there another song in this episode when Concubine Fuyou met the military officer? Was she actually an important person?

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 2
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 2 twice. 6/10.

Maomao was too smart when she figured out the issue. Honestly, there could've been a lot of reasons why people could've been poisoned, not only the smoke from the firewood. Or maybe actually not? It actually sounds weird that many people fell ill after they ate something, so the poison must have spread easily, and it must have happened while or right after they ate dinner at the camp. Also, they had nausea and other symptoms that were able to help her figure it out. And it happened at night, so that might've been another reason why she was able to figure it out. Well, she said it was just her own opinion.

Her co-workers also sympathized with her and were interested in her. She didn't understand how other people saw her. Though, how did other people communicate with her before she ended up in the rear palace? Maybe they didn't care about her at all, and they didn't notice the bandages on her left arm. Or they were already her friends and they knew she liked experiments a lot. So she might actually know how other people saw her.

She also knew what was expensive and what was important. Probably the rear palace was the best place to get medicinal ingredients. And she always figured out what each ingredient was, and how expensive paper was.

I knew who Jinshi was, but from this episode, at least we knew Jinshi was high-ranking in the palace hierarchy. He was able to find and collect precious ingredients from the medicine storehouse, and he was also given a task by the emperor to test the other women's loyalty. That made me realize why he was interested in Maomao. Sure she was unique among women. Why didn't Maomao realize how high-ranking he was, though he talked with Gyokuyou in a friendly way, and frequently? Maybe she thought he was just one of Gyokuyou's favorites?

In the first place, what is the era of this world? At least they have cacao in the rear palace, but I have no idea when it reached East Asia.

In terms of animation, they used lighting pretty well when Maomao first saw the storeroom for medicine ingredients. She stood in a dark room, but it lit up, and then the scene added some visual effects.

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 1
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 1 twice. 7/10. I watched it until the middle of season 2, but this was a complex story so I wanted to start again from the beginning and understand it better.

First of all, the voice actress for Maomao, Aoi Yuki, was so good. How she speaks changes so much with her emotions, even in normal scenes. It showed Maomao's character, too.

In terms of the story, it's still a bit of a mystery why Maomao ended up living in the rear palace after being abducted. Maybe a later episode explains it, but I forgot what it was.

Also, episode 1 showed pretty well what this series was, or who Maomao was. She was a curious cat, who didn't want to get involved in anything terrible like the rear palace or concubines at all. Also, the story misled me about her character a little when she showed she had a complex about her face and her body.

Jinshi already showed he was a person who liked to scheme and worked pretty well, and he was smart as hell. His voice was also so good.

Well, there's nothing else on my mind. As I saw the first time, the backgrounds are absolutely gorgeous, and the clothes and characters are colorful and varied.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 4
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 4 twice. 7/10. New things started slowly, as this series always does.

Geese and Talhand left the place because they were adventurers. I forgot but Roxy was in a party with them so she was also kind to them. And it seems Elinalise would have a wedding with Cliff too, and maybe she was also going to settle there?

Aisha was mature but she still had a childish side and wanted to grow a monster. Or they might have a different sense from ours and have different opinions about monsters. Roxy showed her deep knowledge as she had been an adventurer for a long time. I don't know why Rudeus thought nobody would ever figure out his secret room, even though they had all lived together for a long time. Maybe Roxy also figured it out. It was a great scene, and the voice actor for Rudeus's inner voice did a really good job. It was hilarious. Sugita's voice for an upset, confused man was really good.

Rudeus was also a little hasty to do whatever he thought he needed to do. And he pushed a few things onto other people like Cliff though he changed his mind. But he still pushed Roxy by asking her to teach him King-class water magic. I wasn't sure why Roxy didn't want to teach him but after watching the episode, it was a little clear. She needed almost all of her mana to use that magic, so she didn't want to use it often. Besides, she might not have wanted him to succeed as she knew he was going to cast it. When he was able to pull it off, she smiled but was also sad at the same time. Her expression looked complicated and I couldn't figure it out one way or the other. From her words, she felt down at that time. But she also thought it was like a dream because she could have died in the labyrinth. Well, that made me wonder how many seasons this series will have. Because there were the sword emperor and sword god, I think there will be emperor-class and god-class magic. And Rudeus will probably learn the god-class magic, so it sounds like there's still a long way to go. It also made me wonder how important the labyrinth arc really was for them, and how strong Sylphie and Roxy really are in this series. Or will King-class magic turn out to be nothing special later on?

In terms of animation, the one for the King-class water magic was great. Even though it was water type, the magic was lightning and it was a little off to me. Roxy's one was still good enough to change the weather and blow a large tree, but Rudeus's one was a much bigger spell to collect clouds from a large area. And the lightning came with a lot of clouds, rain, and, well, how can I say it, electricity?

The next episode will probably be the wedding of Elinalise. Also Rudeus wanted to do everything he could, so there will be an episode for him to find his job, like being an adventurer, or analyzing the hydra's skin, perhaps.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 3
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 3 twice. 7/10. This episode was from Rudeus's point of view, and it picked up after the last episode of season 2.

This episode was about a regular, peaceful life. Nothing exciting. Just a normal day as ever. It was funny, and I was relieved, that he still called Roxy his Deity. I thought he stopped at the end of season 2, but he still treated her as his master and his Deity. That was the first word I'd heard from him this season.

But it was still painful to see his left hand because it had been cut off by the hydra.

Sylphy's baby was also born. Forgot her name. Who took care of the baby while Sylphy was at the academy, by the way? Maybe Aisha and Lilia. When they had breakfast at the table, it was actually moving to see them living peacefully and happily after everything that went on over the last 2 seasons. Rudeus was so happy that he didn't even care who was watching, and hugged his wives in public.

I also didn't know Rudeus was sister-obsessed. Was he? Or was this the first episode where he showed it? He acted exactly like Norn's dad. She needed help in season 2 and he took care of her a little, so that might have made him a little emotional. Also, when she turned around, the animation was very detailed and very good. Maybe some animators like her, so it was framed well?

I forgot who Cliff was exactly, except that he had fallen in love with Elinalise. He believed in Millis and in monogamy. So he was furious and Rudeus got a lecture from him like Norn had in season 2, but he understood Rudeus wasn't a member of the Millis Church.

I had been wondering how this anime would handle Rudeus's left hand, and whether there would be healing magic to fix it or not. But the answer was Zanoba's invention. The glove he and Cliff made, the Hand of Zaliff, was so neat, and he was able to use it like his normal hand. Maybe he was going to power up when he got the next one.

The funny part was that he still prayed to his holy grail. Why did he do that? Praying to his own Deity!

The ending animation was completely about Eris. It fit episodes 1 and 2, but which episode will she show up in next? Until then, she might only be in the ending throughout this season.

What will come next, I don't know. But he was a student at the academy and Roxy became the instructor of his class, so something related to her will come. And also, the title of the next episode was "A King-Class Water Mage", so it's probably going to be about how impressive she is. Also, Nanahoshi didn't look well, like she was sick, so there might be an episode related to her, too.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 Episode 2
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 2 twice. 7/10. This episode was again from the point of view of Eris, or rather, Nina.

It seemed Nina spent her whole life on swords, and I guess because of that, she hated losing to Eris. She even tried to find and meet Rudeus because she didn't want to admit he was real, or because she somehow thought she could've beaten him. But after seeing him, it looked like she changed her mind, and her opinion of Eris changed a little. Probably because he was so exceptional and she couldn't imagine even Eris catching up with him. So she might've felt Eris's goal was impossible and the hurdle was too high. It also showed how she and the other members of the Sword God Style didn't know the outside world.

At the training hall, when the Water God came, they were on their guard against Eris the moment she walked in. I thought it meant Eris was so strong compared to them. But after watching the whole episode, it was obvious she didn't even hide her enormous hostility and they were sensitive to it, so that was a reaction to it. Then Eris fought the Water King and lost, but Nina beat her, so their strengths formed a triangle. And after they went over the improvements the Water King suggested, Nina started looking after Eris more. It was partially because Eris also started talking to her more, I guess. And until then, Eris only cared about Orsted and she didn't think about others, except for Rudeus, and even that was infrequent.

So, a few months or years later, in the next training session with the Water King, Eris had changed after getting advice from Nina. She was clean, she didn't rush straight into attacking the Water King, so we were able to see how different she had become in an instant. And when Eris smiled at the Water King, the Water King let her guard down, and Eris landed a hit. And I also forgot a lot because it was in season 1, but Eris was a girl who was very emotional and showed her emotions on her face, not only hostility or desperation toward someone. By the way, I didn't remember Eris was able to use fire magic. Or she just didn't have to use it until this episode? I don't remember.

The action in this episode was also good. The fights between the Water King, Eris and Nina weren't that good, but the action in the fights against the beasts moved pretty well with a fast pace and dynamic camera angles. We could feel the speed and momentum as well as the power when Eris broke the ice cliff. During the training against the Water King, Eris's sword also looked different from the others', and it used the same effect as when she took down the North Emperor, which was unique and indicated she did something different.

Nina saw Rudeus at the best worst time, and she didn't even understand what happened. Well, I also didn't remember what happened at that time, but Rudeus somehow got attention for a duel. Then she only saw the last moment, when he hit Badigadi with his magic and the demon king was blown away. She probably didn't understand it was a deal where the demon king wouldn't dodge and would just take a hit from his strongest magic, so he had as much time as he wanted to cast it. Maybe that left her with an impression of him as a much stronger character than he actually was.

The next episode sounded like it would be from Rudeus's point of view again, so I don't know what'll come.

I watched Jobless Reincarnation season 3 episode 1 twice. 8/10. This episode was completely from Eris's point of view. I actually knew this part of the story because I think I read the manga for it. So I knew what Eris thought and why she left Rudeus behind, but I didn't remember the details.

It was great how desperate she was and she really wanted to be strong. Honestly, she wasn't the type of girl who talks a lot, so I just needed to watch and feel. But after watching it back, I noticed she followed what the Sword God said and did what he instructed her to do. Also, I thought Ghislaine had gone back somewhere because she didn't train Eris, but she was in the Sword God's house. I wondered why. But maybe she followed what her master, the Sword God, said.

I didn't remember the North Emperor from the manga, but that character was also memorable and unique. When Eris started fighting at the gate, she was already exhausted from her training before the fight even started, and she lost. But the next day, she still struggled to fight him, but something happened and she won the sparring match against him. The animation changed to simply blackish colors with only red and blue lines, and she seemed to just jump and swing her wooden sword. Other people called it the Blade of Light, and it probably showed how fast it was. When the Sword God used it on Eris, there was the same animation, too. Speaking of animation, her expression changed very often during the fight. When the North Emperor stood on her sword and pushed it down to the ground, she stopped looking at him. When he counterattacked her at the training hall, she looked surprised for a moment. The animation really cared about the details of everything.

By the way, after her training, she went straight to bed, without changing her clothes. And the next day, she still hadn't changed her training uniform, and it was torn and dirty. She probably didn't care about clothes, only about swords.

I liked the North Emperor's question, "Who is Rudeus?", and the answer was "Rudeus is amazing!" The best answer you could hope for.

Now that I think about Eris, before she met Rudeus, she was already a mad dog and was violent toward everyone, so this showed she didn't change a bit, but just had one single goal in her mind. Also she needed to think about how to fight and move fast by herself for a long time in this episode, so that single-mindedness grew even stronger.

item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 12
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 12. And this was the last episode of season 1. This episode was 6/10, and the entire season was 8/10. This was a great romance anime. This episode covered a few events for Maki and Umi before closing the season, and also showed there might be a next season.

The last episode ended at the beginning of the year, but this episode showed Valentine's Day, White Day, and Umi's birthday. On Valentine's Day, what I thought was that Maki's cooking skill was actually good, so how could she give him a chocolate he would be satisfied with? And in this episode, it was revealed that Umi's cooking skill was not good, or at least she didn't cook often. So she tried to cook something difficult and challenging from the beginning, and failed to do it. I thought Maki should help her make the chocolate together, and he did it so I was kinda satisfied with this small touch.

Then, on White Day, Maki returned something to others. Somehow, there were meanings for gifts and Maki tried to give snacks to each person matching the meaning. For Umi, it was a lot of candy, in both color and amount, instead of cookies.

On Umi's birthday, Maki gave Umi a hairpin, but it looked expensive for a high school student. But it was a good one and Umi wore it. What was good in that scene was that Amami also noticed Umi showing sides of herself Amami didn't know, so she wondered whether Umi had a boyfriend.

And it was the end of their first year of high school. If there is a second season, then the classes will be reshuffled, so this group will be split up.

Overall, this anime was good. There were not many big events, as you would expect from a model slice-of-life anime, but the episodes made progress slowly and steadily. Also, unlike other romance anime, the relationship between Maki and Umi really progressed enough. Interactions between characters were more natural and not awkward, and the main characters didn't talk in their heads too much. So the story was one of the best among romance anime. Well, one weird thing was they loved sharks a LOT.

Animation was also great. There were not many action scenes, but the background art and its animation, and Umi's eyes, were drawn and animated gorgeously. Sometimes, some characters looked weird to me in the animation, but it was acceptable.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 24 (season 2, episode 12)
item.description:

I watched Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 24 twice. 5/10. Story was 3/5, animation was 3/5, voices and audio were 3/5. This episode was the last episode of season 2, and it was more like cooling down than a hot fighting episode.

The most unexpected thing was that Will didn't join the ice faction. I completely expected him to be there, so it was a total surprise to me. At the same time, it made sense, since this way the story can involve not only Elfie but also other Magia Vanders or people in other factions. I thought Will would have the final say on which faction he would join, but from Aaron's perspective, his will counted for nothing.

Colette's obvious jealousy was cute in this episode, too. She showed it in a couple of previous episodes toward Elfie, but she didn't show it to others until this episode. She spent most of her time with Will, I guess, so for her, the situation with Will changed too much. She also tried to confess to Will at the party. But it was out of the blue without any plan, so she never got the chance to do it. And it wouldn't have worked at that party anyway.

Finn, Iris, and Cerridwen's talk explained why Finn let Will join the tower and that answered my original question. I don't know how Finn stayed there or sneaked in there, though. And also, why did Iris call him Invess? Was he a student at the academy or a member of the tower?

Elfie and Will's private talk felt as if Elfie was the heroine. And Workner helped them meet, but if he could do it, why couldn't he have done it even before Will joined the tower? Maybe because she would've gotten out of control. I expected Elfie would talk about Rosty, but she didn't in this episode. Maybe Will won't figure it out for a long time, or maybe never, because she didn't tell him this time. The goal of collecting his lost memories sounded like a good plot, but other than getting help from other mages like Cerridwen, how could he do it? Maybe he would keep remembering out of the blue.

The last scene was, well, expected and unexpected. Obviously, there was a traitor. The voice actor of Headless was hidden. But this story came at the end toward all of the new high mages like this, instead of, I don't know, started somewhere and they would happen to know. Who were the suspects? I have no idea. Maybe the dark faction, Carriot, his assistant, or another faction whose name I didn't even catch were suspicious. We'll see the answer to this in season 3.

Overall, season 2 was great. The battle against the Devander, the battle between Magia Vanders, and Will's awakening were some great episodes. The animation of the battle between Magia Vanders was epic, too. I'll watch season 3. Also, I liked the ending theme. I still couldn't figure out what the child Colette in the ending was about.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 23 (season 2, episode 11)
item.description:
This post includes a spoiler.

I watched Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 23 twice. 9/10. Story was 5/5, animation was 5/5, voices and audio were 4/5. This was a great episode. The main thing was the battle between Zeo and Elfie.

This episode showed how fierce the battle was between two Magia Vanders. And obviously, Ellenor lost to Elfie with ice magic alone, so they both seemed strong. So, the battle was basically one between the cream of the crop and it was worth watching. Zeo's attacks were mostly simple. He used his lightning to move blazing fast, but that was so fast that the animation got good. Like when he threw the wand and then he instantly reached the place where the wand landed, or when the wand came and broke Elfie's clone from an unexpected angle.

Elfie's magic was the exact opposite. She built an ice castle, made a lot of clones, attacked with hundreds of ice shards from every angle, and summoned more ice by drawing a large magic circle. And also, using those remnants, she completely froze his lightning with her ice magic. What was unexpected was that she punched him, with a perfect, anime-style motion, unlike what I imagine a mage would do, and with her magic, the blow landed on him completely. Also, before starting the incantation of her prime magic, she sat on the handrail of the staircase and slid down, and that was so weird. It probably showed her princess-ish behavior but not something you do during a fight.

The animation itself was also great. It wasn't the kind of episode that stops to talk. Characters, buildings, and objects move a lot and fast in most scenes. Of course, when they talked about something, it stopped, but that made a good contrast with the fast-moving scenes. And the entire episode was for this battle alone, and it didn't even end within the episode. The battle between Will and Devander was more like a showcase of Will's Wis ability, so there was some of that, but not at this level. So I was satisfied with this episode.

Story-wise, Elfie put all her effort into fighting him for Will. It was because she had only waited for Will all along, and it was Elfie's turn to do something. This was great, because I thought she hadn't really done much so far and they already had a relationship. Well, it was still a question why they did, but at least, the fact that she stepped up to fight Zeo with all her might changed my opinion about her in this episode. Colette got angry, though. I guess she's already completely lost her chance.

It was also great how Carriot and Ellenor thought and saw the battle. They knew who those two were, so they didn't stop them. And they also noticed that even Zeo got serious once they both used their prime magic. Finn was also smiling and watching the battle, and somehow he knew everything, including Elfie's secret magic. I wonder why he knew how deep Zeo went into the Dungeon, though. He might've been with Zeo? He used to be with the Mage Queen in the past, so I guess he also enjoyed watching mages' battles.

Also, I liked the voice acting of Elfie before the fight started, and Sarissa's shout was great too.

So what's going to happen in the next episode? It looks like Aaron will come down into the venue and butt in. Then Will is going to join Elfie's faction and the season will end shortly.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 22 (season 2, episode 10)
item.description:

I watched Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 22 twice. 7/10. Story was 4/5, animation was 3/5, voices and audio were 3/5.

I was wondering who Cerridwen was. It sounded like Caldron, and now here she was — she was surely Cerridwen. I should've been more confident that it was her, and it made sense that she put in the effort to make Will climb the tower. Because otherwise, it was irresponsible that she just chose him over others' objections to make him climb, and he ended up being a guinea pig. Although, she had so much free time that she didn't have to work as the head of the academy lol But now, it was the opposite. Cerridwen was her true form, and Caldron was a disguise she kept up with aging magic.

She couldn't figure out how to make Will grow stronger for 6 years, but I guess she was finally able to figure something out. Or maybe she could've done it at any time, and it was just that Will had lost his memory and his hair color. So the time had finally come for him.

Also about Finn. It made sense why he handed Will over to Cerridwen now because she had a plan, but then why and how was he there? Did he have that much free time? Well, maybe he did. At least he'd lived for 500 years. He had nothing to do but try to grow the "sword" for him. And he didn't save Will at all even when Zeo attacked him.

In this episode, Will used his Wis from the start. This was the moment he grew stronger again. In the praxis, he got stronger with Wis, and the next step was this time, to use Wis through his own power. What was nonsense was that other people talked up his sword's strength against the Wors Ooze. That thing could be killed with even a tiny amount of magic. Other than Zeo, I felt they exaggerated.

And I was glad to see Colette. She was trying to help Will, and was also jealous of Elfie. Although, she couldn't do anything in the Bloom, so I wanted a scene where she got to do something for Will. Maybe Elfie, who took Will for granted, wasn't someone I liked? I don't know. Well, but her role, and Sion's, Julius's, Lihanna's, and Wignall's. Were they just there to explain what was happening around Will? He was away from them the whole time, too.

Kreutz was simply nonsense in this episode.

Now I realized, I liked the ending a lot. "Reach for the Light," I guess. I am still wondering what that scene with Colette as a child was about, but maybe that scene was not included in season 2.

I watched I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 9. 7/10. This episode included

  1. Maki was accepted to join the Christmas party
  2. Maki talked with his mother about the truth about their living expenses
  3. Maki visited Umi's house

The main part of this episode was how Maki reacted to seeing Umi's family while they had a normal conversation like a family does, and that reminded Maki of his family's past Maki's past with his family was short, simple, but still sad enough for a character of a slice-of-life anime. And his reaction was quiet, but he couldn't stop crying — exactly like his character, who cared about others and who didn't attack or blame others. And Umi was, well, maybe the ideal girl who chased him regardless of whether he ran away or not, and calmed him down and stayed with him. It was well drawn that she thanked him in earlier episodes that he meant a lot to her, and also, Maki didn't recognize it. From Maki's perspective, she was the first friend who was nice to him and got along with him, so probably he thought it was nothing special. Now, come to think of it, he didn't have any friends because he moved schools from time to time, so his family was everything to him, and I can imagine the divorce of his parents hurt a lot.

The other parts are minor. Early in this episode, Amami was unwilling to see Umi's brother, but this episode didn't show how creepy his behavior was. Only Umi described what his behavior was like. Umi's father was very tall, a head taller than Maki, but like Maki, he was kind, and Umi's mother always led the conversation. It wasn't such a shock that Maki's mother didn't say anything about the living expenses she was trying to earn without using the money she got from Maki's father. I still don't exactly know what happened between them, but she might be kinda stubborn, or hasn't forgiven what he did. In the scene where Umi caught Maki after he ran away, the background was someone's house decorated cleanly and brightly for Christmas, so that brightness and beauty made it clear they were moving forward in a good way. Before he ran away, it was a plain street without good lighting, so at that time, it showed how depressed Maki was.

There were a few things wrong about the nitty-gritty. Maki started running away and Umi was trying to catch up. But they were just eating dinner and went out suddenly, so running in such a condition should hurt them and it was hard to run. They were emotional and they didn't care about that, though. Also, when Umi was trying to make Maki sleep in her lap, the camera was from Maki's eyeline. But it looked at Umi, though he was obviously looking in a different direction, so I wanted the previous cut to be consistent.

Well, anyway, what I wanted to say was they were a match made in heaven, even compared to any other anime. I don't know what Maki will do in the next episode, but he'll probably invite his parents to the school's Christmas party and try to get them to work out their arguments. And they would start living together, but I guess it won't happen.

item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 5
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 5. 9/10.

  • Story and characters: 5/5
  • Design and animation: 3/5
  • Voices and audios: 3/5

The earlier part of this episode was that Umi started talking about her past and the reactions there, and then Umi and Maki talked in a classroom. The later part was that Umi talked with Amami on the roof with Maki again, and then they hung out in Maki's room before they called it a day. I didn't expect this episode was still on the school festival day, and I thought it had finished in the previous episode, but I was wrong.

I like the overall story in the episode. This episode showed how Umi really felt about Amami, and it wasn't very simple. It was love and hate. I also wondered why she talked with the other 2 girls, but her past explained it well, and that was also sad but at the same time a pretty natural thing, too, because human relationships can change over time. And that explained why Umi and Amami at least went to that high school, instead of moving up to the high school attached to their middle school, which they could have entered without taking an exam. Although, I wasn't sure why other girls also followed them and entered the same school. They were at least really friends with Amami, supposedly.

Also, when Maki found Umi alone in a classroom after she left the roof, she cried but didn't cry aloud and kept talking with him. I thought she might've cried a lot as characters in other anime often do, but she didn't, and that was good, and more genuine. Moreover, she still cared about Amami at that time, so she really was kind to her.

I wondered why Amami asked those 2 things of Umi and Maki, but then I think she wanted Maki to be the one who never left Umi, perhaps? Maybe she also had a complex feeling at that time because she wanted to be the best friend of Umi. I didn't fully understand what she was trying to do when she was playing a ghost, but maybe she wanted to see how Umi talked with him and wanted to feel the difference, and just got her head around it.

Umi showed her more decisiveness and initiative than Maki at the end of this episode. He wasn't familiar with being around people, so he wasn't very brave, and the episode showed these things well even at the end. And she also still was a little playful. Anyhow, overall, episode 5 wrapped up one arc of the plot so far. Maybe this was the first volume of the original light novel, I guess. It was a clean, well-organized, convincing story that brought the characters to life.

For animations, I felt like when Umi and Amami were at the 3rd year grade, their heads were too big as a character design. Then when they became 1st years in middle school, they were almost identical to how they look in high school. Also, Umi's eye color is red, and nothing was said about it, though the color of Amami's eyes was mentioned and some kids stayed away from Amami because of her eye color. Which one is weirder. Well, that's anime world.

What's going to come? Well, I was glad that Amami also started liking Maki like regular rom-coms do, but it seemed that she cared about him because she perhaps started noticing that Umi was hanging out with him. So, that won't come, I suppose. If it's an ordinary rom-com anime, then another person who falls in love with Umi or Maki will appear and a few of them will start doing something. Lightning animation

This section was written on July, 2026.

Next animation was the one I made by following steps:

1. Base layer

  1. Create new solid layer
  2. Add an effect Advanced Lightning and set following properties:
    • Glow Settings > Forking to 0, to remove lightning hairs
    • Change other settings on Glow settings and Core Settings to get what you want
  3. Animate the layer by
    • Clicking the stop watch on the Conductivity State
    • Set the different values of Conductivity State in a few key frames

2. Core lightning layer

This will change the color of the core of the lightning to the color you want It's because core and glow settings use screen-style blend instead of normal blend. So if the core color is a bright color like white, this isn't necessary.

  1. Duplicate the first layer.
  2. Set the properties on the new layer:
    1. Set Glow Settings > Radius to 0
    2. Set Core Settings > Color to the color you want
  3. On the previous layer, set Core Settings > Radius to 0

Then I was able to get what I wanted. The video did pre-compose the new layer, add Fill effect and change the color of the effect, but I didn't see any difference.

Variations of Advanced Lightning

The above lightning only goes from top to bottom, because the Lightning Type is Direction. We can get some different animations with different lightning types. Here are a few examples I played around.

However, for more details about Advanced Lightning effect, next video was the most helpful for me to walk through the details:

Bouncey

Here is the lightning animation with Bouncey Lightning Type.

Anywhere

If it's set as "Anywhere", the lightning goes everywhere. The example of the animation is next:

Rough steps to create this was

  1. Add new solid layer with Advanced Lightning effect, and set
    1. Lightning Type to Anywhere
    2. Set Conductivity State to make this animated
    3. Set Forking to 50%
    4. Set Core Settings and Glow Settings as we want to
    5. Enable Composite on Original
    6. Set Outer Radius to make the effect enough to go a lightning from one edge to another
  2. Duplicate the Advanced Lightning 3 times and on each set Origin to put them on 4 edges

item.title: Random thoughts after re-watching Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 1

I watched the Saga of Tanya the Evil episode 1. I watched this series a long time ago, and I liked it, but I forgot most of the story, so before the season 2, I decided to watch again.

This anime was mainly for a war similar to the World War 1, and the Empire was from Germany, and the Republic was from France. But as it's a fantasy, there is a unit who can use a magic and they can even fly and use a magic power into a gun.

The main character Tanya Degurechaff was in the Empire side. The episode 1 started from the trench warfare of the west line in the Empire. The first, it showed how cruel the front line was and some soldiers were depressed due to the trench and some soldiers were dead. They even called there a living hell.

In the Tanya's unit, some soldiers had come to the front to fight and didn't even obey the order of the commander Tanya. Obviously, they didn't like her. She tried to dismiss them, but they didn't follow that either, so she ordered them to move to a rear. Well, obviously, she liked rules, orders, and didn't like exceptions, motivations, etc. She was like half as tall as other soldiers, so she was really a kid.

In the another day, Visha, who was one in the Tanya's unit, was exhausted and couldn't follow Tanya while flying to the front line. Tanya found out she was behind and gave her harsh words that she should leave or catch up then Visha followed catching up. Later, using Visha's exhaustion as an excuse, Tanya tried to ask the commander to avoid the fight. But Visha volunteered and insisted she was able to fight despite what Tanya said. So Visha was serious, and one who is a patriot, obviously.

Then Tanya decided to take out a Republic company, the 105th, iirc. That company had defeated the Empire's magic soldiers a lot so they underestimated any of them. But Tanya dodges any attacks, tried to take down its commander and failed, but still did so for some soldiers, and then fly to the 10,000 meters, which Republican's couldn't do. In order to fly high, I guess they should at least have the ability to deal with an atmospheric pressure, able to breathe with low oxygen, and deal with cold temperature, I guess. I guess breathe and temperature aren't usually a problem for these stories so I assume they were also able to deal with them by their magics. So, Republican's couldn't fly because of the atmospheric pressure. Then Tanya used telepathy to ask soldiers to surrender, and obviously they didn't, so she used some strong magic that could blow the entire company out. It was not as strong as an atomic bomb, but obviously it was way stronger than the normal bombs or guns and can kill not only by the explosions but also by carbon dioxide. Some person even called her the Devil of the Rhine, not only from the enemies but also from within. And then Visha found out that Tanya ordered two men to go to the rear because they were going to be dead and Visha was scared about it. Well, she was definitely an intimidating girl for sure.

I noticed, this episode started that Tanya was like a fairy in the battle field, from what Visha thought, then ended that she was the monster in the form of a little girl.
